description: Translation glossary for QuantEcon lectures (English to Malayalam). v0.6.0 encodes the third inline review round (44 suggestion blocks on lecture-python-programming.ml#13, matplotlib; dispositions in QuantEcon/project-translation reports/2026-09-18-ml-matplotlib-review-disposition.md): two everyday words the editor moved to Malayalam twice each (multiple, explicit), two software-action verbs kept in the light-verb form (remove, label), and — new in this version — `style_examples`: sentence pairs from the three lectures the editor has reviewed, exactly as he approved them, rendered after the terms so the translator sees his comma rhythm, verb aspect and clause order rather than being told about them. Held for his answers on ml#22: provide, prefer, draw, available, and the rule-2 boundary itself. v0.5.0 pins the four words the editor answered on lecture-python-programming.ml#12 (2026-09-01): already, example / examples, name (the noun for a bound identifier; the act of naming stays പേര്), and work (light-verb form, work ചെയ്യുന്നുണ്ടോ) — the items held back from v0.4.0. Validated by the native-speaker packet reply 2026-08-03 (experiments/ml-benchmark/DISPOSITIONS.md): C1 confirmed keep-English for the 34 most frequent unpinned terms — deliberately NOT pinned, the policy holds unpinned (203/203 terms measured) — and C2/A8 pinned the software-interface verbs (click, option, set, type, press) that machine output had transliterated; terminology extractors never propose interface verbs, so nothing else protects them. v0.4.0 adds the ordinary words the second inline round moved back to English (useful, provide, exist, automatically, create, improve, full, stage, answer, successive, plus the line/lines pin the #273 regeneration flagged — 118 suggestion blocks on lecture-python-programming.ml#7, dispositions in QuantEcon/project-translation reports/2026-09-01-ml-functions-review-disposition.md) and four everyday words he moved the other way (straightforward, contrived, limited, facilitate). v0.3.0 added the instructional verbs the reviewer's first inline PR review round moved back to English (cover, break down, refer, repeatedly — 100 flags on lecture-python-programming.ml#1, dispositions in QuantEcon/project-translation reports/2026-08-17-ml-python-by-example-review-disposition.md). Policy: keep-English-dominant — technical/domain terms keep their English form (ml == en), and ordinary English content words (everyday adjectives, adverbs, nouns) also usually stay in Latin script per packet A1; Malayalam is generated mainly as grammatical connective tissue around the English words. The few translated 'everyday' entries below (country, year, ...) are deliberate exceptions with a natural in-use equivalent, not an open class to extend. Where ml == en, the term is intentionally kept in English. Malayalam values for the everyday words are taken from native-speaker reviewer Adisankar Manoj Thanuja's worked examples. Grammatical function words (we, two, each, more, before, ...) are deliberately NOT pinned here: they inflect with Malayalam grammar and are handled by the prose rules in language-config, not term-level consistency.
